full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Articles 1 to 4 , placed in Part I of the Constitution, deal with the Union and its territory. Article 1 describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States' — this single provision does two jobs at once: it fixes the country's name , and it fixes the type of polity . On the name question, the Constituent Assembly had no unanimity — some members wanted the traditional name Bharat , others the modern name India — so the Assembly settled on a compromise combining both: 'India, that is Bharat' .
full_companion_paragraphs.telugu_exact: Articles 1 నుండి 4 , రాజ్యాంగం Part I లో — Union, దాని territory గురించి చెబుతాయి. Article 1 India ను, అంటే Bharat ను, 'Union of States' అని వర్ణిస్తుంది, 'Federation of States' అని కాదు — ఈ ఒక్క నిబంధనే రెండు పనులు చేస్తుంది — దేశం పేరు నిర్ణయిస్తుంది, polity రకం నిర్ణయిస్తుంది. పేరు విషయంలో, Constituent Assembly లో ఏకాభిప్రాయం లేదు — కొందరు సంప్రదాయ పేరు Bharat , కొందరు ఆధునిక పేరు India కోరారు — చివరకు రెండింటినీ కలిపి 'India, that is Bharat' గా స్థిరపడ్డారు.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: On the polity question — the country is described as a 'Union' even though its Constitution is federal in structure. According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar , the phrase 'Union of States' was preferred to 'Federation of States' for two reasons: one , the Indian Federation is not the result of an agreement among the states, the way the American Federation was; and two , the states have no right to secede from the federation. The federation is a Union precisely because it is indestructible — the country is one integral whole, divided into states only for the convenience of administration.
full_companion_paragraphs.telugu_exact: Polity ప్రశ్న విషయంలో — దేశం రాజ్యాంగం federal structure అయినా దాన్ని 'Union' అని వర్ణిస్తారు. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar ప్రకారం, 'Union of States' ను 'Federation of States' కంటే రెండు కారణాల వల్ల ఎంచుకున్నారు — ఒకటి , American Federation లా India Federation రాష్ట్రాల మధ్య ఒప్పందం ఫలితం కాదు; రెండు , రాష్ట్రాలకు federation నుండి secede అయ్యే హక్కు లేదు . Federation ఖచ్చితంగా indestructible కాబట్టే ఇది Union — దేశం ఒకే integral whole, పరిపాలన సౌలభ్యం కోసమే రాష్ట్రాలుగా విభజించారు.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Per Article 1, the territory of India falls into three categories: (1) territories of the states ; (2) union territories ; and (3) territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any time. The names and territorial extent of states and UTs appear in the First Schedule of the Constitution. The Constitution's provisions on states apply uniformly to all of them — but the special provisions under Part XXI (applicable to Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Karnataka) override the general provisions relating to states as a class; further, the Fifth and Sixth Schedules contain separate provisions for administering scheduled areas and tribal areas within states. Currently, there are 28 states and 8 union territories.
full_companion_paragraphs.telugu_exact: Article 1 ప్రకారం, India territory మూడు వర్గాలుగా ఉంటుంది — (1) states territory; (2) union territories ; (3) India ప్రభుత్వం ఎప్పుడైనా సంపాదించే territory. States, UTs పేర్లు, పరిధి రాజ్యాంగం First Schedule లో ఉంటాయి. రాజ్యాంగ నిబంధనలు states కు ఒకేలా వర్తిస్తాయి — కానీ Part XXI ప్రత్యేక నిబంధనలు (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka కోసం) సాధారణ నిబంధనలను override చేస్తాయి; Fifth , Sixth Schedules రాష్ట్రాల్లోని scheduled areas, tribal areas పరిపాలన కోసం ప్రత్యేక నిబంధనలు ఇస్తాయి. ప్రస్తుతం 28 states, 8 union territories ఉన్నాయి.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Notably, the 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India' — the latter includes only states, while the former includes not only the states but also union territories and territories that may be acquired in future. States are members of the federal system , sharing a distribution of powers with the Centre; union territories and acquired territories, by contrast, are directly administered by the Central government.

States federal system లో సభ్యులు, Centre తో అధికార పంపిణీ పంచుకుంటాయి; union territories, సంపాదించిన territories దీనికి భిన్నంగా Central government చే నేరుగా పరిపాలించబడతాయి .

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Being a sovereign state, India can acquire foreign territories according to modes recognised by international law — cession (following a treaty, purchase, gift, lease or plebiscite), occupation (of territory hitherto unoccupied by a recognised ruler), conquest or subjugation . full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Article 2 empowers Parliament to 'admit into the Union of India, or establish, new states on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit'. full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: It is thus clear that the Constitution authorises Parliament to form new states or alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states without their consent . In other words, Parliament can redraw the political map of India according to its will — the territorial integrity or continued existence of any state is not guaranteed by the Constitution. Hence, India is rightly described as an 'indestructible union of destructible states' — the Union government can destroy states, but state governments cannot destroy the Union. The USA , by contrast, guarantees the territorial integrity of a state constitutionally — its federal government cannot form new states or alter existing borders without the consent of the states concerned — hence the USA is described as an 'indestructible union of indestructible states' .

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Does Parliament's power to diminish the area of a state (under Article 3) include the power to cede Indian territory to a foreign country ? This question came up before the Supreme Court via a Presidential reference in 1960 . The Central Government's decision to cede part of a territory known as the Berubari Union (West Bengal) to Pakistan led to political agitation and controversy, necessitating the reference. The Supreme Court held that Parliament's power to diminish a state's area under Article 3 does not cover cession of Indian territory to a foreign country. Hence, Indian territory can be ceded to a foreign state only by amending the Constitution under Article 368 . Consequently, the 9th Constitutional Amendment Act (1960) was enacted to transfer the Berubari territory.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: India and Bangladesh share a land boundary of approximately 4,096.7 km . The India-East Pakistan boundary was originally determined by the Radcliffe Award (1947) ; disputes arising from it were addressed via the Bagge Award (1950) , then the Nehru-Noon Agreement (1958) — but the division of the Berubari Union was itself challenged before the Supreme Court, leading to the 9th Amendment, 1960 discussed on the previous page. Due to continuous litigation and other political developments, the 9th Amendment could not be notified in respect of the erstwhile East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) territories. On 16 May 1974 , an Agreement on demarcation of the land boundary was signed, but it was not ratified — since it involved transfer of territory requiring a constitutional amendment, and precise on-ground identification of the areas to be transferred was still needed. These outstanding issues — undemarcated boundary, adverse possessions, and exchange of enclaves — were finally identified and resolved by a Protocol signed on 6 September 2011 , an integral part of the 1974 Land Boundary Agreement, prepared with the support and concurrence of the state governments of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and West Bengal.
full_companion_paragraphs.telugu_exact: India-Bangladesh land boundary సుమారు 4,096.7 km . full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: At independence, India comprised two categories of political units — British provinces (under direct British rule) and princely states (ruled by native princes, subject to British paramountcy). The Indian Independence Act (1947) created two separate dominions, India and Pakistan, and gave princely states three options: join India, join Pakistan, or remain independent. Of 552 princely states within India's geographical boundaries, 549 joined India; the remaining 3 — Hyderabad, Junagarh and Kashmir — refused, but were integrated in due course: Hyderabad by police action , Junagarh by referendum , and Kashmir by the Instrument of Accession .

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: The integration of princely states with the rest of India was a purely ad hoc arrangement. There had long been a demand from different regions — particularly South India — for reorganisation of states on a linguistic basis . Accordingly, in June 1948 , the Government of India appointed the Linguistic Provinces Commission under the chairmanship of S.K. Dhar to examine this feasibility. The commission's December 1948 report recommended reorganisation on the basis of administrative convenience rather than language — a recommendation that created much resentment.

Commission డిసెంబర్ 1948 report language బదులు administrative convenience ఆధారంగా reorganisation సిఫారసు చేసింది — ఇది చాలా అసంతృప్తి సృష్టించింది.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: The creation of Andhra State intensified demands from other regions for states on a linguistic basis. This forced the Government of India to appoint, in December 1953 , a three-member States Reorganisation Commission under the chairmanship of Fazl Ali (other members — K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru ) to re-examine the whole question. It submitted its report in September 1955 , broadly accepting language as the basis of reorganisation — but rejecting the theory of 'one language-one state' . Its view was that the unity of India should be the primary consideration in any redrawing of political units. It identified four factors relevant to any reorganisation scheme: (1) preservation and strengthening of the unity and security of the country; (2) linguistic and cultural homogeneity; (3) financial, economic and administrative considerations; (4) planning and promotion of the welfare of the people, in each state and the nation as a whole.
full_companion_paragraphs.telugu_exact: Andhra State ఏర్పాటు ఇతర ప్రాంతాల నుండి linguistic basis పై states డిమాండ్ ను తీవ్రతరం చేసింది. దీంతో India ప్రభుత్వం డిసెంబర్ 1953 లో ఈ మొత్తం ప్రశ్నను మళ్ళీ పరిశీలించడానికి Fazl Ali ఛైర్మన్ షిప్ లో (ఇతర సభ్యులు — K.M. Panikkar , H.N. Kunzru ) 3-member States Reorganisation Commission నియమించింది. సెప్టెంబర్ 1955 లో report సమర్పించింది, language ను reorganisation ఆధారంగా broadగా అంగీకరించింది — కానీ 'one language-one state' theory ను తిరస్కరించింది. India ఐక్యతే political units redrawing లో primary consideration గా ఉండాలని దాని అభిప్రాయం. Reorganisation scheme కోసం నాలుగు factors గుర్తించింది — (1) దేశ ఐక్యత, భద్రత సంరక్షణ-బలోపేతం; (2) linguistic, cultural homogeneity; (3) financial, economic, administrative పరిగణనలు; (4) ప్రజా సంక్షేమం ప్రణాళిక-ప్రోత్సాహం, state, జాతి రెండింటిలోనూ.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Till 1947 , Sikkim was an Indian princely state ruled by the Chogyal . After the lapse of British paramountcy, Sikkim became a 'protectorate' of India, whereby the Indian government assumed responsibility for its defence, external affairs and communications. In 1974 , Sikkim expressed a desire for greater association with India — the 35th Constitutional Amendment Act (1974) introduced a new class of statehood by conferring on Sikkim the status of an 'associate state' of the Indian Union, via a new Article 2-A and a new 10th Schedule (containing the terms and conditions of association). This experiment did not fully satisfy the people's aspirations — in a 1975 referendum, they voted for abolition of the Chogyal institution and for Sikkim to become an integral part of India. Consequently, the 36th Constitutional Amendment Act (1975) made Sikkim a full-fledged state ( 22nd state), amending the First and Fourth Schedules and adding a new Article 371-F for Sikkim's special administrative provisions; it also repealed Article 2-A and the 10th Schedule that the 35th Amendment had added.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: Till 2019 , the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir had its own constitution, and thus enjoyed a special status by virtue of Article 370 of the Constitution of India. In 2019, this special status was abolished by a presidential order known as 'The Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019' , which superseded the earlier order known as 'The Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 1954'. The 2019 order extended all provisions of the Constitution of India to J&K as well. Further, the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 bifurcated the erstwhile State of J&K into two separate union territories — the UT of Jammu and Kashmir , comprising all districts of the erstwhile state except Kargil and Leh , and the UT of Ladakh , comprising those two districts. Thus, the number of states and UTs increased from 14 and 6 (in 1956) to 28 and 8 (present) — see Table 6.3 in the revision/summary notes.

full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: The names of some states and union territories have changed over time. United Provinces was the first state renamed — Uttar Pradesh , in 1950 . full_companion_paragraphs.english_exact: J&K statehood restoration — pending, not yet granted: The Union government has repeatedly stated an intention to restore full statehood to J&K (as distinct from Ladakh, which remains a UT), but as of this date this restoration has not happened — J&K remains a union territory (with its own elected legislature, unlike Ladakh). This is an active, unresolved political and legal issue: J&K's Chief Minister has publicly pressed for early restoration of statehood; opposition parties have repeatedly demanded it; and petitions seeking a court-directed timeline for restoration have been before the Supreme Court, with the Court at one point directing the Centre to respond on the matter. Students should treat "J&K = still a UT, statehood restoration still pending" as the correct current position — not that it has already reverted to statehood.
